paper_title: Searching for solar axions using data from the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory
notes: Solar-axion search via axiodissociation of deuterium (a+d->n+p) at SNO. Headline result (abstract, text p.4, Fig.1): excludes the isovector axion-nucleon coupling |g^3_aN| = (1/2)|g_an - g_ap| between 2e-5 and 1e-3 GeV^-1 at 95% C.L. for axion masses up to ~5.5 MeV; the upper edge (~1e-3 GeV^-1) is a solar-trapping cutoff, so the constraining boundary is the flat lower edge g^3_aN = 2e-5 GeV^-1, essentially mass-independent (flux ~ (p_a/p_gamma)^3 ~ 1) up to the 5.5 MeV kinematic reach. Two points span the flat exclusion; low-mass edge taken from Fig.1 (~1e-22 eV). Per task 'isovector rule', reported as the single canonical coupling with the other set to zero: setting g_ap=0 gives g_an^paper = 2*g^3_aN = 4e-5 GeV^-1. Paper eq.(1) uses L = (1/2) g_an^paper (d_mu a) nbar gamma^mu gamma5 n (g in GeV^-1), so canonical dimensionless g_an = m_n * g_an^paper = 0.9396 GeV * 4e-5 GeV^-1 = 3.76e-5 (equivalently g_an=2 m_n * g with g=g^3_aN=2e-5). The identical bound applies to g_ap (AxionProton) if g_an is instead set to zero; the Fig.1 y-axis is labelled |g_an|, so neutron chosen. Not a dark-matter search (dm_density_assumed=null).
